name: Exterior Painting Cost per Square Foot in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What is a realistic price range per square foot for professional exterior painting in Los Angeles County, and which factors move a quote to the high end?
mainEntity.text: What is a realistic price range per square foot for professional exterior painting in Los Angeles County, and which factors move a quote to the high end?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners often see wildly different exterior painting quotes in Los Angeles County and struggle to know what is fair. Instead of chasing a single number, think in ranges. Basic, low-prep repaints on simple one-story homes with sound stucco and minimal woodwork will land at the lower end of typical per-square-foot pricing. Costs rise as prep becomes more labor intensive: heavy scraping, sanding, patching stucco, or addressing peeling fascia and eaves all add hours. Multi-story homes, steep lots, or limited side-yard access may require scaffolding or lifts, pushing labor and equipment charges higher. Complex architecture with many angles, trim profiles, railings, and decorative elements further increases time on-site. Using top-tier exterior paints, elastomeric coatings, or specialty primers for chalky stucco or tannin-rich woods adds material cost but can extend repaint cycles. HOAs with strict color schemes and multiple sample rounds, or older neighborhoods with historic features, may also require more meticulous work. Ask each painter to break out labor, materials, access equipment, and repair allowances separately. If one quote is significantly lower, confirm what level of prep and product they are actually including so you can compare apples to apples.
acceptedAnswer.description: Professional exterior painting in Los Angeles County commonly ranges from roughly a few dollars to several dollars per square foot, with higher pricing driven by extensive prep, stucco repair, complex architecture, access challenges, premium paints, and strict HOA or historical requirements. The home’s condition and design typically matter more than size alone.
